title: Lazio's Metano Premium Just Flipped — First Time All Year
dek: A weekly look at how Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano moved in Lazio on November 5th, and what the longer trend reveals once you compare it to the national average.
executive_summary: Lazio drivers paid an average of €2.006 per liter for self-service Benzina on November 5th, down slightly from €2.007 the day before, while Gasolio dipped fractionally to €2.234. GPL told a very different story, jumping 1.60% day-over-day to €0.796 — the sharpest single-day move of the four fuels tracked. Metano held perfectly flat at €2.097, a day on which none of the region's reporting stations changed their posted price. Against the national same-day averages (Benzina €2.018, Gasolio €2.257, GPL €0.799, Metano €2.088), Lazio stayed cheaper on three of four fuels and was only marginally pricier on Metano.

Zoom out to the weekly data tracked since July 20, and the real story is Metano. Lazio's price has climbed 27.3% over that span (from €1.607 to €2.047), which sounds dramatic until you see the national trend: Italy's average self-service Metano price has risen 36.6% in the same window. Lazio entered the tracking period with a notable Metano premium over the rest of the country — 7.2% more expensive in the week of July 20 — and has spent the autumn watching that premium shrink to nothing. By the week of November 2nd, Lazio's regional average (€2.047) slipped fractionally below the national figure (€2.049) for the first time in the dataset. Benzina and Gasolio, by contrast, have moved almost in lockstep with the national picture all year, while GPL has been the odd one out in the opposite direction, with Lazio's increase outpacing the national one and the gap widening further just in the last month.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina: A Quiet Day, A Flat Year
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Lazio averaged €2.0058 per liter on November 5th, down €0.0014 (-0.07%) from €2.0072 the previous day — a negligible move. Served-pump Benzina followed the same pattern, easing from €2.1510 to €2.1492. Nationally, the same-day self-service average was €2.0176, meaning Lazio drivers paid about 0.6% less than the rest of Italy for Benzina on November 5th, continuing a pattern that has held for most of the autumn.

Looking at the weekly self-service averages, Lazio's Benzina price has risen 2.20% since the week of July 20 (€1.964 to €2.007 by the week of November 2), almost identical to the national move of 2.25% over the same span (€1.976 to €2.020). The two series have essentially tracked each other all year, including a shared mid-September spike — both Lazio and Italy peaked in the week of September 21 (Lazio €2.153, national €2.167) before easing back roughly 7% into October. What's notable is how unremarkable Benzina has been relative to the other three fuels this year: it's the only one of the four where Lazio and the national average have stayed within half a percentage point of each other in essentially every tracked week.

fuel_sections.heading: Gasolio Eases Back From Its September Peak
paragraphs: Gasolio self-service in Lazio ticked down to €2.2343 on November 5th from €2.2354 the day before, a -0.05% move, with served-pump prices following the same direction (€2.3898 to €2.3889). The national same-day self-service average was €2.2567, putting Lazio about 1.0% below the country as a whole — Lazio's largest discount of the four fuels tracked today.

Since the week of July 20, Lazio's Gasolio has risen 3.84% (€2.154 to €2.237 by the week of November 2), just behind the national increase of 3.89% (€2.175 to €2.259). Both series peaked in the week of September 21 — Lazio at €2.350, nationally at €2.374 — before falling back roughly 4.5% into November. The timing of that peak-and-retreat lines up almost week-for-week between Lazio and the rest of Italy, which points to Gasolio pricing here being driven by the same national wholesale cycle rather than anything regional.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL Is the Fuel to Watch in Lazio
paragraphs: GPL was the day's biggest mover: Lazio's self-service average jumped 1.60% to €0.7961 on November 5th from €0.7836 the day before, while served-pump prices rose a smaller 0.90% (€0.7966 to €0.8038). Even after that jump, Lazio stayed cheaper than the national same-day self-service average of €0.7994.

The weekly data shows this isn't a one-day blip. Lazio's GPL has climbed 5.04% since the week of July 20 (€0.742 to €0.780 by the week of November 2), outpacing the national rise of 4.20% (€0.759 to €0.791) over the same span. More strikingly, the gap has widened specifically over the past month: Lazio's GPL is up 3.63% since the week of October 5th alone, versus 2.71% nationally. GPL actually fell in both Lazio and nationally through August and September, bottoming out around €0.724–0.735 in late September, before reversing hard into October and November — and Lazio's reversal has been the sharper of the two.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano's Regional Premium Has Vanished
paragraphs: Metano held exactly flat in Lazio on November 5th at €2.0965 self-service, with served-pump prices edging up slightly from €2.1027 to €2.1101. The national same-day self-service average was €2.0878, meaning Lazio was marginally more expensive — by about €0.009, or 0.4% — a reversal of the position it held for most of the year.

This is the standout trend of the whole dataset. Since the week of July 20, Lazio's Metano has risen 27.3% (€1.607 to €2.047 by the week of November 2) — a large move on its own, but dwarfed by the national increase of 36.6% (€1.500 to €2.049) over the same period. Lazio started the tracking window with a clear Metano premium over the rest of Italy (+7.2% in the week of July 20) and has watched that premium erode every month since, until the week of November 2nd, when the national average (€2.049) edged just above Lazio's (€2.047) for the first time in the data. The pace of the national catch-up has actually accelerated recently — national Metano is up 10.05% since the week of October 5th alone, versus just 5.14% in Lazio over the same four weeks — so if the pattern holds, Lazio could soon be the cheaper-than-average region for Metano, a status it hasn't held once since tracking began.

network_section.heading: Station Network: 2,373 Registered, 2,099 Reporting
paragraphs: Lazio has 2,373 registered fuel stations in the MIMIT registry as of November 5th, of which 2,099 reported at least one price that day — a reporting rate of 88.4%. That's down marginally from 2,100 reporting stations (88.5%) the day before, out of an unchanged 2,373 registered.

Nationally, 21,653 of 23,939 registered stations reported prices on the same day, a rate of 90.5% — meaning Lazio's reporting compliance runs about two points below the national average. A reporting rate in the high-80s to low-90s is typical across the dataset and mostly reflects stations that simply didn't update their price that particular day rather than closures; it's one reason the daily averages above are best read as directional rather than exact to the last reporting station.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made — Entirely Without a Spreadsheet
paragraphs: Everything above — the raw price pull from MIMIT's open data feed, the regional rotation that picked Lazio today, the week-over-week trend analysis, and the prose you're reading — is produced automatically every morning by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. No analyst opens a spreadsheet, pastes in a CSV, and manually drags down a formula; no one writes the commentary by hand. A scheduled agent pulls the data, runs the same statistical comparisons every day, and drafts a fresh report grounded in that day's actual numbers.

The region-of-the-day rotation itself is deterministic, not editorial: it cycles alphabetically through Italy's 20 regions keyed to the calendar date, so every region gets equal coverage over a 20-day cycle and the choice is auditable rather than hand-picked. Compare that to the traditional way this kind of report gets made — a person checking a fuel-price website once a week and updating a shared spreadsheet — and the difference isn't really about effort saved, it's about consistency: this pipeline produces the same depth of analysis every single day, for every region, without ever skipping a week because someone was busy.

Use the scope picker to switch to Region and pull up Lazio's full history, drop down to Province or Municipality for hyperlocal pricing, or flip to another Operator/Brand to see how a specific chain is pricing nationally — the same underlying data and weekly trend view behind today's report is available live, for whichever slice you choose.

pull_quote: Lazio's Metano used to cost 7% more than the rest of Italy — as of this week, for the first time since tracking began, it's cheaper.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Lazio.

The number that stood out: Lazio's Metano has historically cost more than the Italian average — as much as 7% more back in July. This week, for the first time since I started tracking, that premium flipped: the national average (€2.049/L) edged above Lazio's (€2.047/L). Benzina and Gasolio barely moved day-over-day, while GPL quietly became the region's fastest-rising fuel, up 3.6% in the past month alone.

Fuel Dashboard is a live, self-updating dashboard tracking fuel prices across all of Italy — every brand, region, province and municipality — refreshed every morning straight from MIMIT's open data feed. No manual downloads, no spreadsheet upkeep. Take a look: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

This entire pipeline — the data pull, the regional trend analysis, even the write-up itself — runs unattended every morning, built with Claude Code. A year ago this would have meant a person checking a government site once a week and updating an Excel sheet by hand. Now it's code that never skips a day and never makes a typo. That's the real case for building with AI tools right now: not "AI writes your report," but "AI builds the thing that keeps writing it correctly, every day, for free."
